### bao2026diverge
- **Citation:** Honglin Bao, Siyang Wu, Xiao Liu, Sida Li, Shiyun Cao, James A. Evans. 2026. Contemporary AI lacks the imagination to diverge or negate in science. arXiv 2606.08251 (cs.CY, also cs.AI; v1 6 Jun 2026, v3 10 Aug 2026). https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.08251
- **Verification:** verified. Title, author order, year and category match the arXiv API. The text is laid out in journal style but names no venue, so it is an arXiv preprint [full text, judgelit_diverge.md].
- **What it is:** Authors of 121,640 recent preprints in biology, medicine, chemistry and social science rated LLM-generated ideas derived from their own papers on novelty, feasibility, probability of being true and favourability of adoption. Ideas came from 26 LLMs. The study also compares automated evaluators (LLM-as-a-judge and reward models) with the expert ratings, post-trains a Qwen3-14B reward model on the ratings, and analyses 39 million papers (2010-2025) with agent-based simulations.
- **Numbers we might cite:**
  - 6,749 scientists returned 25,139 rating sets [abstract]. Ratings are on a 1-9 scale [full text].
  - "no model spontaneously proposes null hypotheses" [abstract]. The null-hypothesis classifier has 99.5% cross-validated accuracy [full text].
  - LLM judges (Gemini 2.5 Flash, DeepSeek R1, o4-mini Deep Research): "no model exceeded r = 0.35 on any dimension" (Pearson vs human ratings) [full text]. The abstract says automated evaluators "agree weakly with expert judgment".
  - Within-scientist pairs (5,000 held out): o4-mini Deep Research judge 41% / 55% / 43% (feasibility / probability / novelty); Skywork-Reward-V2-Qwen3-8B 53% / 55% / 49% [full text].
  - Asking for extreme scores "only increases the standard deviation of ratings by 0.33 on a 1-9 scale" [full text].
  - Qwen3-14B reward model: beats SOTA models "by up to 27%" [abstract]; the full text gives "up to 27% (+14 percentage points on average across three dimensions)" over the strongest baselines [full text]. Per-dimension pairwise accuracy (novelty / feasibility / probability): biology 69% / 62% / 67%, social science 64% / 62% / 67% [full text]. Reviewer-agreement reference: 61.0% ± 0.1% on 26,731 OpenReview submissions to 46 venues [full text].
  - After ChatGPT's release, the share of papers with zero null claims rises (on average 74% in medicine, 77% in social science) [full text].
- **Where V9 uses it:** not cited in V9.
- **Properties (for the comparison table):**
  - Executed/automatic ground truth: no. Expert ratings.
  - Graded 'nothing found' answers: no. Null hypotheses are a category of generated idea, not graded absence answers.
  - Planted or known-rank tool failure: no.
  - LLM judge evaluated against ground truth: yes, against expert ratings (Pearson r, pairwise accuracy).

### sahoo2025reject
- **Citation:** Devanshu Sahoo, Manish Prasad, Vasudev Majhi, Jahnvi Singh, Vinay Chamola, Yash Sinha, Murari Mandal, Dhruv Kumar. 2025. When Reject Turns into Accept: Quantifying the Vulnerability of LLM-Based Scientific Reviewers to Indirect Prompt Injection. arXiv 2512.10449 (cs.AI; v1 11 Dec 2025, v2 15 Dec 2025, v3 6 Jan 2026). https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.10449
- **Verification:** verified. Title, author order (Mandal seventh, Kumar eighth), year (v1) and category match the arXiv API. No venue. Version note: v3 is a rewrite of v2. It has a new abstract with the 86.26% figure, adds a Limitations section, and drops v2's "RQ4 remote code execution" section [full text, judgelit_reject.md].
- **What it is:** Appends adversarial text to paper PDFs as invisible 1pt white text on the last page, converts the PDFs to Markdown (MinerU), and scores them with an LLM reviewer under a strict JSON rubric (7 criteria × 0-5, total 0-35, 7 decision buckets). It tests 15 attack strategies in three classes (obfuscation, context reframing, fabricated authority) on 13 models. The data are 200 papers for 8 open models and a 50-paper subset for 5 proprietary models. It introduces the Weighted Adversarial Vulnerability Score (WAVS).
- **Numbers we might cite:**
  - "decision flip rates of up to 86.26% in open-source models" [abstract]. This figure is the largest percentage-point increase in acceptance rate (mistral-small, Cls1DRA, Table 3), not the critical Reject-to-Accept flip rate [full text]. The critical flip rate is over 14% in open models; on proprietary models the maximum is about 0.8% per model (Gemini 2.5 Pro) and 1.6% per strategy (v2 Figs 13, 15) [full text]. Exact open-model peak unconfirmed: judgelit_reject.md says "over 14%" in its findings and "near 14%" in its caveats.
  - Average score increase (0-35 scale): Maximum Mark Magyk +13.95 (mistral-small:22b), +12.59 (gemma3:27b); Disguise and Reconstruction +13.87, +13.53 [full text].
  - Proprietary models: GPT-5 near zero everywhere. The largest proprietary spike is Gemini 2.5 Pro +2.54, and its largest acceptance-rate increase is 13.04 points [full text].
  - Expert Endorsement injections lowered some scores (gemma3 −3.95) and changed no proprietary acceptance rate (Table 3: 0.00 for all five) [full text].
  - Single runs; no temperature reported; no defence tested [full text].
- **Where V9 uses it:** not cited in V9.
- **Properties (for the comparison table):**
  - Executed/automatic ground truth: no. ICLR accept/reject status enters only as a WAVS risk weight.
  - Graded 'nothing found' answers: no.
  - Planted or known-rank tool failure: no. Hidden text is planted in the input document, not a tool failure.
  - LLM judge evaluated against ground truth: no. No baseline accuracy of the un-attacked reviewer against human decisions is reported.

### ma2026
- **Citation:** Tianyi Ma, Hanzhang Qin, Ruihao Zhu, Jierui Zuo. 2026. "Best-Arm Identification with Generative Proxy." arXiv 2607.06879. https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.06879
- **Verification:** verified (verify_batch_6, from Semantic Scholar and alphaXiv; the arXiv API returned 429 there). arXiv check in this pass: v1 (8 Jul 2026), title and four authors match, no venue. verify_batch_6: the paper is not about abstention or biased proxies.
- **What it is:** The paper studies fixed-confidence best-arm identification in which each costly reward pull comes with a cheap proxy score (for example, from an ML model or an LLM) whose correlation ρ with the reward is unknown and is learned online. It proposes PROBE, a phase-elimination algorithm that keeps an OLS-based upper certificate on the residual variance. It tests PROBE on synthetic instances and on an auto-loan pricing replay with LLM and tabular proxies (abstract).
- **Numbers we might cite:** the oracle sample complexity improves by the residual variance factor 1 − ρ². PROBE is δ-PAC and attains the known-correlation oracle sample complexity up to a constant multiplicative factor and a constant additive calibration cost (abstract). There are no empirical numbers in the abstract.
- **Where V9 uses it:** not cited in V9. Earlier drafts: cited once each in V8, V7, V5, V4_user and BEST. CITATIONS_REPORT f lists it as optional for §7 Proxies, "not for abstention or for a biased proxy".

### tiwari2026decodability
(proposed key; a draft entry with this key exists in the scratchpad RELATED_WORK_NOTES.md, per sec08 R08-14 / R08-26; not in either bib)
- **Citation:** Devesh Tiwari, Camille Davis, Shivank Sinha, Talia Weaver, Aditya Shah, Maheep Chaudhary. 2026. "Decodability is Not Causality: Dissociating Probe Readouts from Behavioral Drivers via SAE Decomposition." COLM 2026 Workshop on Agent Behavior. arXiv 2609.18080 (cs.AI). https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.18080
- **Verification:** verified. arXiv check: v1 (16 Sep 2026), six authors match, no comment or journal_ref. The PDF header on every page reads "Published at COLM 2026 Workshop on Agent Behavior" (alphaXiv read in this pass, and again in the verifier pass). The workshop was not checked against a COLM page (unresolved).
- **What it is:** The paper decomposes a deployed True/False truth probe (TTPD, Bürger et al. 2024) into Gemma Scope SAE features (16,384 features, layer 20 of Gemma-2-9B-Instruct, instructed truth/deception setting of Long et al. 2025). It ranks the features by probe alignment and by the gradient sensitivity of the model's True/False margin, then ablates shared, probe-only and random feature sets under a coherence gate. Appendix A.2 applies the same workflow to a released reward-hacking code probe ("AlignmentResearch/diverse-deception-probe-qwen3-8b", layer 20 of Qwen3-8B, from Taufeeque et al. 2026) on MBPP-Honeypot-style examples, with a Qwen-Scope layer-20 SAE.
- **Numbers we might cite (each checked on the PDF in this pass):**
  - **Error-term margin, App. A.2, Table 7 (p. 17):** raw probe margin 3.84 (100%); SAE reconstruction 1.00 (26%); SAE error vector 2.84 (74%). Text (p. 16): "Only 26% of the raw probe margin was preserved by the SAE reconstruction, while 74% lay in the reconstruction error." **The 74% value is confirmed** (re-read on the PDF in the verifier pass). It belongs to the A.2 reward-hacking code probe on Qwen3-8B, not to the main TTPD study. The paper states that this probe "did not pass the SAE-substrate verification" and treats the setting as a boundary case (pp. 16-17).
  - App. A.2 (p. 17): ablating probe-aligned SAE features flips about one third of predictions scored on the reconstruction, and near zero on raw activations. The top-50 sparse mask flips 32.7% of reconstruction predictions vs 2.1% of raw ones; the raw flip rate peaks at 4.5% for top-100.
  - Main study (Table 1, §5.1): the top 16/50/100/200 probe features share 2/7/12/22 features with the gradient ranking (chance 0.02/0.15/0.61/2.44); Spearman ρ = 0.10; about 12% overlap (abstract).
  - Main study (§5.2): shared features flip 13-27% of outputs (0.130 at 16, 0.269 at 54); probe-only 6% (0.061); random 1% (0.010).
  - Abstract: activation-aware selection flips behaviour 17.6% vs 6.1% for the probe's geometric top features. The dissociation holds across five seeds and a held-out split (abstract; Table 2: shared 0.105 ± 0.017, probe-only 0.059 ± 0.016, random 0.010 ± 0.002 over five seeds; held-out 0.122 / 0.085 / 0.010).
  - §3.7: the SAE reconstruction has mean cosine 0.89 with the layer-20 activations (normalized reconstruction MSE 0.21). Shared-set ablation removes 5.7% of the residual-stream norm, and the mean KL is 0.11 nats for the shared set.
- **Where V9 uses it:** not cited in V9. sec08 R08-14 holds the same numbers.
- **Properties (for the comparison table):** executed/automatic ground truth? yes for the ablation effects (behaviour flips are measured on the model). Graded 'nothing found' answers? no. Planted or known-rank tool failure? no planted failure. A.2 reports a probe whose margin lies mostly (74%) in the SAE error term, found by measurement. LLM judge evaluated against ground truth? no.
- **Found in:** not in gaps_*.md, judgelit_*.md or 00_collected.md; requested by the task. Existing mention: facts/sec08_related_comparison.md R08-14, R08-26, R08-27 item 10.
